details: CONFIRMED (reproduced). build_findings (lib/relay_verdict.py:784) lets review_paths be empty whenever
relay_inert.absorbed(wt, head) is non-empty. With no review, the only findings are Q1 (if the branch took an item) and
_merge_findings, which (line 680-690) only names own files that some merge commit's diff (merge^1..merge) touched.
A file the branch changed in an ordinary commit is in `own` but in no merge diff, so it gets no M finding. record_check
then accepts an empty status list, the verdict is open 0, and step_mark accepts the mark (no own file changed since it).
Design 3.3 says the merge check is for a train and its findings are "one per combined file"; it assumed the train's own
files are exactly the combined files. That holds only while the train has no commit of its own, and never holds for a
stacked branch, which is the commonest branch with an absorbed branch (T12). The owner's rule "Never no review" and the
design's "A change to a file is never dropped without a check" are both broken: any agent on a stacked branch can now
land its own code by recording an empty check. Severity HIGH: breaks a promise of the review gate on ordinary use
(stacked branches exist today; a train fixer committing a gate fix on the train is the design's own red-train path).
Size: 30 agent minutes (the rule plus two tests).
failing_case: 1. Stacked: wt/p ready (lib/f.py, gate, mark open 0); wt/s made from wt/p commits lib/g.py ("unreviewed"), gates it.
`relay check findings -C <s>` with no --review prints only "Check of <sha>" and "Item: none" (no finding at all);
`record_check` with `review = []` and no [[status]] records a mark with open 0; merge.judge("wt/s") returns None
(allowed). lib/g.py lands on master with no review and no verdict on it.
2. Train: wt/a and wt/b ready with disjoint files; train-1 merges both, then a plain commit on the train adds lib/new.py.
Same: findings list empty, `review = []` records open 0, the train is allowed. lib/new.py was never reviewed or checked.
Expected: a merge check lists every own file of the branch that no absorbed branch covers (lib/g.py, lib/new.py) as a
finding the checker must give MET to, or `review = []` is refused when the branch has own non-inert files that came from
its own (non-merge) commits; the stacked branch S needs its review as today (design 3.2 T12: "S still needs a mark for
its own file", reached by a real review, not an empty check).
fix_hint: In build_findings, when review_paths is empty: compute own = relay_inert.changed(wt, fork, head, own=True,
absorbed=ab) and refuse ("a merge check is only for a branch whose own files all come from merging ready changes") when
any file of own is not touched by a merge whose second parent is an absorbed tip or the default branch; or emit an M
finding for every file of own (not only those a merge touched) when no review is given. Add the two probe cases to
pass_cases: - Stacked S on ready P, S commits lib/g.py: `relay check findings -C <s>` with no --review is refused ("at least one review")
or lists lib/g.py as a finding; a record with `review = []` and no status for it is not open 0 / is refused.
- Train of a and b plus a direct train commit adding lib/new.py: the merge check lists lib/new.py (or is refused); a mark
with no verdict on it does not let the train land.
- T14 as today: a train with only the combined file lib/shared.py lists exactly M1 for it; M1 MET with `review = []`
records a mark the hook accepts.
- T1 as today: a train with no combined file and no own commits needs no mark at all.
- A normal branch with no absorbed branch: `review = []` refused as today.
reason: tests/test_merge_train.py:479 (stacked own commit) and the direct-commit test pass; fail at dd1b136; pass-case tests pass.
findings.summary: a check with no review is allowed on any branch that holds a ready branch, and lists only files a merge touched, so code committed directly on that branch lands with no review and no check

details: CONFIRMED (reproduced). The design's answer to the design review's F1 (HIGH) was the covered-file conditions plus test
T10 "Refused, naming lib/f.py". The build delivers only condition 2 in the file list (relay_inert.changed shows lib/f.py
against master), not the refusal: step_mark (merge.py:196) compares each mark with the head, and lib/f.py at S's mark
already equals the head, so no own file changed since the mark and the mark passes. _merge_findings only lists files the
merge's diff merge^1..merge touched, and a resolution that keeps "ours" leaves lib/f.py out of that diff, so the
checker is never asked either. docs/plans/review-gate.md 7.7 now records this as "Known gap, from before the train",
and the test T10 asserts only the list ("only the list shows it here"). The gap is older than the change, but the
design promised to close it ("A change to a file is never dropped without a check": T10) and the brief said to build
the design exactly and to ask about anything it leaves open; dropping a promised test case was not raised as a
question. Master's change to a file can be lost with no verdict on it, which a person reaches by any hand resolution.
Size: 30-45 agent minutes (an M finding for a file the merged side changed whose result differs from the merged side,
and a step_mark rule that a merge after the mark that drops the other side's change needs a newer check).

Master commits Q (lib/f.py line 1 -> "Q one"). S takes master, the conflict is resolved with `checkout --ours lib/f.py`

no M finding for lib/f.py. Expected (design 3.2, 3.6 and T10): refused, naming lib/f.py; after a check of S with M1 for
fix_hint: In _merge_findings, for each merge of the default branch (or of an absorbed tip), list a file the second parent changed
since the merge-base (merge-base(merge^1, merge^2)..merge^2) whose result at the merge differs from merge^2's version
and is own: that is a dropped or combined change, an M finding. In step_mark, after the chosen mark, refuse when such
a merge exists after it with no newer mark. Then make T10 assert the refusal and the allow after M1 MET. Or ask the
owner to accept the gap and say so in the report.
pass_cases: - The T10 sequence above: judge("wt/s") refuses naming lib/f.py; `relay check findings -C <s>` lists M1 for lib/f.py;
after a mark of S whose check has M1 MET, judge allows.
- The same sequence where S's merge of master combines lib/f.py cleanly (Q changed another line): allowed with S's
mark as today, or with the M1 the merge produces as today (no new refusal for a clean take).
- T12 as today: stacked S on ready P, nobody else changed lib/f.py: S's mark for lib/g.py alone lets it land.
- T11 as today: a train commit setting a combined file to one rider's version is refused.
